meta.description: Marc Andreessen wrote it: "In short, software is eating the world," Wall Street Journal, 20 August 2011 — and said it as early as a 2000 interview.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Software is eating the world'?
meta.ogDescription: Verified: Marc Andreessen, Wall Street Journal essay, 20 August 2011. Quote Investigator traces the line back to an October 2000 interview.

answer.label: Written by
answer.authorDates: b. 9 July 1971 · Mosaic & Netscape co-creator, venture capitalist
answer.sourceLine: These are Andreessen’s own words. The sentence — printed as “In short, software is eating the world.” — closes the opening of his Wall Street Journal essay “Why Software Is Eating The World,” published 20 August 2011; the WSJ article page is preserved as a print-to-PDF capture ↗. Quote Investigator ↗ documents him using the line earlier still, in an October 2000 interview.

author.name: Marc Andreessen
author.heading: Who wrote it
author.metaLine: Born 1971 · Netscape co-founder & Silicon Valley venture capitalist
author.bio: Marc Andreessen (born 9 July 1971 in Cedar Falls, Iowa) co-wrote Mosaic, the browser that put inline images on the web, then co-founded Netscape. In 2009 he co-founded the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz with Ben Horowitz. He is one of the few technologists whose off-hand formulations become industry doctrine — and this is the most quoted of them.

misattribution.heading: What gets garbled
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Andreessen is not in doubt. What travels badly is the date, the exact wording, and the line’s many descendants.

items.why: The 2011 essay made the phrase famous, but Quote Investigator ↗ records Andreessen saying “Software is eating the world” in a CRN interview with Ben Horowitz published 9 October 2000, in the Loudcloud era.

items.who: The headline quoted as the quote
items.why: The essay is headlined “Why Software Is Eating The World”; the sentence inside it reads “In short, software is eating the world.” Variants such as “software will eat the world” also circulate — Quote Investigator lists them ↗ alongside the primary form.
“Software is eating the world, but AI is going to eat software” is Nvidia’s CEO, speaking to MIT Technology Review on 12 May 2017 ↗ — not Andreessen.

misattribution.truthLine: Andreessen wrote it, in the Wall Street Journal of 20 August 2011 — and, on the evidence Quote Investigator gathered ↗, had been saying it for years before that.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: When Andreessen wrote it, the argument was contrarian: technology stocks were trading at low price/earnings ratios and commentators were asking whether Facebook-era valuations were a second bubble. His answer was that the market had the story backwards — that software companies were about to take over large parts of the wider economy, industry by industry.

The line survived because it is a thesis compressed into five words. It became shorthand for a whole decade of investment logic, and then a template: every subsequent hype cycle has borrowed the grammar of “X is eating Y.”
detailsBody: Writing on the tenth anniversary, CIO Dive ↗ called the piece “oft-quoted” and reported that enterprise software spending had grown from roughly $269 billion to about $600 billion over that period.
Not everyone agreed at the time or since; a VentureBeat column of October 2011 ran under the flat rebuttal “Software is not eating the world,” as Quote Investigator notes ↗.
